page: Microsoft Azure F16amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 1890 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 10% at 3354.98. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall within the average range. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is highly efficient, scoring in the top 10% at 15.98 GB/sec, while multi-threaded decompression and gzip compression show strong performance in the top 25%. For lightweight AI workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds of 420.78 tokens per second using a small 135M LLM model.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation, high memory density, and substantial local storage, this server offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of a GPU. The absence of hyperthreading ensures predictable compute performance per core. This configuration is well-suited for memory-intensive databases, data processing pipelines, caching layers such as Redis, and medium-scale web serving applications.
